hindu_nasatya.name: Holds the Madhuvidya, the honey-doctrine of life-restoring medicine learned from Dadhyañc
hindu_nasatya.notes: With his twin he obtained the secret honey-knowledge from the sage Dadhyañc by replacing his head with a horse's head; thereby the Aśvins became the physicians of the gods.

hindu_prithvi.name: Forms with the sky-father Dyaus the world-parent pair that engenders and upholds all beings
hindu_prithvi.notes: Hymned in the Rigveda jointly as Dyāvāpṛthivī, the dual sky-and-earth, the broad parents who hold creatures, gods, and the cosmic order between them.

hindu_ulupi.name: Moves between the serpent-realm and the surface as a Naga princess, half-maiden and half-serpent
hindu_ulupi.notes: Daughter of the Naga king Kauravya; commands the waters and depths of the Naga world and draws Arjuna into it.

hindu_ulupi.name: Commands the use of the Naga life-restoring gem to revive the slain
hindu_ulupi.notes: In the Ashvamedhika Parva she has the Mṛtasaṃjīvanī gem brought from the Naga realm and instructs Babhruvāhana to lay it on the fallen Arjuna, restoring him to life and lifting the Vasu-curse upon him.

hindu_uparichara_vasu.name: Moves through the air at will in the crystal celestial chariot given by Indra
hindu_uparichara_vasu.notes: His byname 'the upward-mover' derives from this gift; Indra rewarded his austerities with a sky-going crystal car that let him traverse the heavens like a god.

hindu_satyavati.name: Secures the Kuru succession by invoking the niyoga levirate, summoning Vyasa to beget heirs
hindu_satyavati.notes: After her sons by Shantanu die heirless, she calls her firstborn Vyasa to father Dhritarashtra and Pandu upon the widowed queens, on which the whole later epic turns.

hindu_parashara.name: Promulgates the Vishnu Purana, the foundational Vaishnava cosmology recited to Maitreya
hindu_parashara.notes: Tradition credits Parashara as the original speaker of the Vishnu Purana, later redacted by his son Vyasa; he expounds creation, the yugas, and royal genealogies to his pupil Maitreya.

hindu_parashara.name: Founds the science of horoscopy as reputed author of the Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra
hindu_parashara.notes: Hindu astrological tradition regards Parashara as a father of Jyotisha; the Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra is ascribed to him.

hindu_parashara.name: Kindles the rakshasa-destroying sacrifice to avenge his devoured father, then relents at Vasishtha's word
hindu_parashara.notes: Learning a rakshasa had eaten his father Shakti, he begins a sacrifice consuming the rakshasas by hundreds; his grandfather Vasishtha and the sage Pulastya persuade him to halt it.

sources.reference: Mahabharata, Adi Parva; Vishnu Purana, Book 1

hindu_vidura.name: Embodies Dharma in mortal form, born of Yama under the curse of the sage Mandavya
hindu_vidura.notes: Yama, cursed by Mandavya for an unjust impalement, is born as the maidservant's son Vidura; at his death his spirit merges back into Yudhishthira, Dharma's other son.

hindu_vidura.name: Counsels kings in statecraft and righteousness, delivering the Vidura-niti to Dhritarashtra
hindu_vidura.notes: His discourse on the duties of rulers and the conduct of the wise (Udyoga Parva 33-40) is preserved as the Vidura-niti; he repeatedly warns against the war.

hindu_vibhishana.name: Forsakes his unrighteous brother to take refuge with Rama, choosing dharma over kin
hindu_vibhishana.notes: Rebuked for opposing Sita's abduction, he crosses to Rama's camp, is granted asylum, and is consecrated future king of Lanka before the war.

hindu_vibhishana.name: Reveals the secret weaknesses of Lanka's defenders, guiding the vanaras to victory
hindu_vibhishana.notes: His knowledge of rakshasa rites and warriors lets Rama counter Indrajit's sacrifices and identify the foes; he performs Ravana's last rites after the battle.

hindu_sumali.name: Wins Lanka and dominion over the three worlds through the unbreakable bond and boon of Brahma
hindu_sumali.notes: With his brothers Mālyavān and Māli he gains from Brahma indomitable strength and brotherly union, seizes the city of Lanka built by Vishvakarman, and rules until driven by Vishnu into Pātāla.

sources.reference: Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara Kanda (sons of Sukesha)

hindu_shatrughna.name: Slays the demon Lavanasura with a Vishnu-empowered shaft and founds the city of Mathura
hindu_shatrughna.notes: His name, 'slayer of foes', is borne out when he kills Lavana, nephew of Ravana, at Madhupura and is crowned king there, refounding it as Mathura.

hindu_sampati.name: Discerns Sita's prison across the ocean with far-sight and directs Hanuman's host to Lanka
hindu_sampati.notes: Wingless on the Vindhya shore, the aged vulture tells the searching vanaras that Sita is held a hundred yojanas across the sea in Ravana's Lanka; on rendering this service in Rama's name his wings regrow.

hindu_parikshit.name: Is revived in the womb by Krishna after Ashvatthaman's Brahmastra burns the embryo
hindu_parikshit.notes: Aśvatthāmā's weapon strikes the unborn child in Uttarā's womb; Krishna restores him, whence his name 'the tested one'. As sole Kuru survivor he succeeds Yudhishthira and rules sixty years.

sources.reference: Mahabharata, Sauptika Parva; Bhagavata Purana, Book 1

hindu_vasudeva.name: Bears the infant Krishna across the flooding Yamuna to safety as his chains fall away
hindu_vasudeva.notes: Imprisoned by Kamsa, on Krishna's birth his fetters open and the prison guards sleep; he carries the child through the parting, Shesha-sheltered Yamuna to Gokula and exchanges him for Yashoda's daughter.

sources.reference: Bhagavata Purana, Book 10; Vishnu Purana, Book 5

hindu_ravana.name: Rudra-vina played in worship of Shiva

sources.reference: Shaiva tradition; Ravana as devotee-musician of Shiva

hindu_vibhishana.name: Mace borne as warrior-prince of Lanka

hindu_nasatya.gloss: The wondrous / accomplisher of marvels (of the twin pair)

hindu_satyavati.gloss: She whose fragrance carries a yojana

hindu_surya.name: Arghya to the rising sun
hindu_surya.notes: Devotees offer water libations to the rising sun and recite the Surya-gayatri and Aditya-hridaya; the salutation-sequence Surya-namaskara accompanies the rite.

sources.reference: Aditya Hridaya (Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda); Surya worship tradition

hindu_surya.name: Chhath Puja
hindu_surya.notes: In the eastern Gangetic plain devotees fast and stand in water to offer arghya to the setting and rising sun and to Chhathi Maiya; one of the most rigorous solar observances.

sources.reference: Chhath Puja regional tradition (Bihar, Jharkhand, eastern UP)

hindu_surya.name: Ratha Saptami
hindu_surya.notes: Celebrates the sun's chariot turning northward; great solar temples such as Konark and Modhera enshrine Surya as a chariot drawn by seven horses.

sources.reference: Surya temple tradition; Konark Sun Temple

hindu_soma.name: Somayajna (soma-pressing sacrifice)
hindu_soma.notes: The soma stalks are pressed with stones, strained into the graha cups, and offered; the Agnishtoma is the model soma-sacrifice, with morning, midday, and evening pressings.

hindu_uparichara_vasu.name: Indra-dhvaja (Indra's banner festival)
hindu_uparichara_vasu.notes: The Mahabharata traces the royal festival of raising and worshipping Indra's flagstaff to Vasu, who first planted the bamboo pole Indra gave him; kings thereafter erected and decked the pole yearly for Indra's worship.

sources.reference: Mahabharata, Adi Parva (origin of the Indra-festival)

hindu_vibhishana.name: Veneration as a Chiranjivi (deathless one)
hindu_vibhishana.notes: Granted long life and unwavering devotion by Brahma, Vibhishana is counted among the chiranjivis and venerated in Vaishnava and temple tradition (notably at Sri Ranganatha shrines) as the righteous rakshasa-devotee.

attributes.name: Crescent moon set in the matted locks (chandrashekhara)
attributes.notes: The waxing crescent in his jata marks his lordship over time; with it the descending Ganga streams from his hair.

attributes.name: Vertical third eye on the brow that incinerates with its glance
attributes.notes: The eye of fire that burned Kama to ash; emblem of inner vision and destructive power.

attributes.name: Tiger- or elephant-skin garment and ash-smeared body
attributes.notes: Clad in the hide of slain beasts and smeared with cremation ash (vibhuti), marking his ascetic mastery over death.

attributes.name: Matted ascetic hair (jata) bearing the river Ganga
attributes.notes: He breaks the fall of the descending Ganga in his locks; the epithet Gangadhara.

sources.reference: Ramayana, Bala Kanda (descent of Ganga); Puranas

sacredAnimals.name: Nandi, the white bull mount couchant before his shrine
The serpent-king Vasuki coiled about his neck

sacredPlants.name: Rudraksha beads (seeds of Elaeocarpus) worn as rosary
Dhatura flowers and cannabis offered to him

attributes.name: Two-armed beside Shiva, four-armed alone, fair-complexioned and crowned
attributes.notes: As the gentle Devi she is shown benevolent and golden (Gauri), bearing lotus, mirror, or rosary; often holding a bowl of food as Annapurna.

sacredAnimals.name: Lion (or tiger) vahana, emblem of her fearless power

sacredPlants.name: Lotus held in hand and as her seat

attributes.name: White-clad goddess seated on a lotus, playing the vina
attributes.notes: Robed in white for purity, four-armed, holding vina, book (pustaka), and rosary (akshamala); embodies speech, learning, and music.

sacredAnimals.name: Hamsa (swan/goose) vahana, discerner of milk from water
Peacock shown attending her in some depictions

sacredPlants.name: White lotus, her seat and emblem of transcendence

attributes.name: Resplendent standing figure holding a lotus in each hand
attributes.notes: Haloed solar god riding his chariot, a full-blown lotus in either raised hand; in Northern images shown booted, of Iranian-influenced type.

attributes.name: Chariot of seven horses driven by the legless charioteer Aruna
attributes.notes: The seven steeds are named for the Vedic metres; red Aruna, personified dawn, holds the reins; twelve wheels mark the months.

sources.reference: Konark Sun Temple iconography; Puranic tradition

sacredPlants.name: Lotus, opened by and emblematic of the sun

attributes.name: White-bodied deity bearing a mace, hare-marked (shashanka)
attributes.notes: Pale lunar god holding a club, the moon marked with the figure of a hare; he waxes and wanes as the cup of the gods' nectar.

sacredAnimals.name: Chariot drawn by antelopes (or white horses)

attributes.name: Conch-pale lord bearing the noose, beneath a white umbrella
attributes.notes: Crystalline-complexioned god of waters holding the pasha (noose) to bind wrongdoers; the white parasol arose at the ocean-churning. Guardian of the western quarter.

sacredAnimals.name: Makara, the part-crocodile sea-creature he rides

attributes.name: Swift god on a shining chariot of many horses, white banner flying
attributes.notes: Rigveda describes him borne by two, forty-nine, or a thousand white-and-purple steeds; first to receive the soma offering.

sacredAnimals.name: Antelope/deer (or gazelle) as his mount in later iconography

attributes.name: Radiant bejewelled maiden uncovering her breast, opening heaven's gates
attributes.notes: Hymned as a beautiful dancer-bride who reveals herself with the daily light, drives away darkness, and rouses all life to its tasks; daughter of the sky (Divo Duhita).

sacredAnimals.name: Ruddy cows / red-gold horses drawing her chariot

attributes.name: Youthful horse-headed (or horse-borne) twin in a golden three-wheeled chariot
attributes.notes: The Aśvins appear before dawn as radiant horsemen; their car is golden and triangular, swift as thought, bringing healing and treasure.

sacredAnimals.name: Horses, in name and chariot the Aśvins' defining animal

attributes.name: Humped white bull reclining on a platform, gazing toward Shiva's sanctum
attributes.notes: Set in the Nandi-mandapa on the temple's central axis facing the linga since at least the early Agamas; the ideal devotee fixed on the lord.

attributes.name: Anthropomorphic Nandikeshvara: bull-faced or four-armed gatekeeper with axe and antelope
attributes.notes: At many South Indian Shaiva temple doors he stands as gatekeeper, sharing Shiva's third eye, crescent, and matted locks.

attributes.name: Dark-/blue-complexioned princely archer bearing bow and quiver
attributes.notes: Shown standing with the Kodanda bow, often in the Rama-darbar flanked by Sita, Lakshmana, and the kneeling Hanuman.

sources.reference: Vaishnava Rama iconography; Ram Darbar tradition

sacredPlants.name: Tulasi (holy basil) offered in his Vaishnava worship

attributes.name: Golden-hued queen risen from the furrow, returning into the earth
attributes.notes: Ploughed up by Janaka and at the end received back by her mother Earth; iconographically the demure consort at Rama's left.

sources.reference: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda and Uttara Kanda

attributes.name: Earth-goddess holding a blue lotus, also figured as a cow
attributes.notes: As Bhudevi she clings to the tusk of the Varaha boar who lifts her from the waters; the cow-form expresses her all-nourishing abundance.

sacredAnimals.name: Cow, image of the all-bearing nourishing earth

attributes.name: Lustrous jasmine-skinned maiden with lotus-petal eyes, consort of Kama
attributes.notes: Embodiment of erotic delight; depicted beside Kamadeva and the spring-god Vasanta, sharing his parrot and flower-bow imagery.

attributes.name: Ten-headed, twenty-armed rakshasa king, crowned and bejewelled
attributes.notes: Born ten-headed and twenty-armed; a learned Shiva-devotee and Veda-master, shown bearing many weapons, burned in effigy at Dussehra.

attributes.name: Crowned vanara (monkey) king, garlanded to be told from Vali in battle
attributes.notes: At Rama's instruction he wore a flower-garland (gajapushpi) so Rama could distinguish him from his identical brother and shoot Vali.

attributes.name: Mighty vanara wearing Indra's golden pendant that swelled his strength
attributes.notes: His father Indra's golden chain/pendant augmented his energy in combat; he could drain half a foe's strength when faced directly.

attributes.name: Naga princess, half-maiden and half-serpent
attributes.notes: Dwells in the serpent-realm beneath the waters; bears the hood-marks of the Naga kindred.

attributes.name: Giant divine vulture, wingless until his wings regrow at Rama's service
attributes.notes: Son of Aruna and elder brother of Jatayu; his pinions were scorched shielding Jatayu from the sun and regrow on directing the vanaras to Sita.
